title: Model fallback governance and regional readiness crosswalk
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Synthesize competitive model landscape research into a concrete governance playbook for fallback routing and regional readiness. Deliverables: (1) a decision matrix that maps customer profile + SLA -> preferred fallback trajectory (model variant, region, quantization level), (2) a minimal telemetry signalset and policy thresholds that trigger automatic fallback or operator alerting, and (3) an experiment plan to validate customer-visible latency and quality regressions across fallback paths.
acceptance_criteria: Decision matrix completed with at least 6 enterprise profile rows and mapped fallback paths for NA/EU/APAC
Telemetry signalset documented and implementable by infra (list of metrics + thresholding rules)
Experiment plan with statistical power calculations and synthetic workloads submitted to SRE for scheduling
Stakeholder sign-off from Console PM, Runtime Eng lead, and Security on the governance principles
tasks: Compile up-to-date model capability matrix (latency, cost, known failure modes) across top 8 open models and Redwood-verified variants
Interview 3 enterprise customers about acceptable quality vs latency trade-offs for critical flows
Draft fallback policy prototypes (strict SLO-first, cost-aware soft-fallback, conservative quality-first)
Define telemetry signals (p99 latency, rejection rate, token drop anomalies, semantic-quality-sampled-score) and sketch alerting rules
Work with Runtime Eng to map technical feasibility of cross-region fallbacks and quantization variant swaps
Design canary experiments to compare primary vs fallback routes for 3 representative workloads

2026-02-18 - Marco Hernández: Initial matrix v0 uploaded to Drive. Key observation: two open-source model families show 20-40% slower decode for long contexts when quantized aggressively — needs special-case handling.
2026-02-22 - Priya Singh (Console PM): Reviewed telemetry list; asked for token-level cost delta metric to be included so Console can show cost impact per fallback event.

2026-02-25 - SRE Liaison (Liam O'Connor): Cross-region fallback feasibility: cold-start risk for KV caches will add ~80-120ms; proposed solution: warm-prefix caching + probabilistic routing during region drain.
2026-02-28 - Security (Elena Markov): Note: cross-region PII routing requires customer opt-in; added requirement to surface opt-in flag in Console and API contracts.
2026-03-01 - Marco Hernández: Updated experiment plan with power calc for user-sentiment sampling; next: align on sample prompts and quality rubric.
decisions: Use three canonical fallback trajectories: (A) In-region model variant downgrade (quantized but same region), (B) Cross-region primary-equivalent model with warm-prefix cache, (C) Graceful degradation to short-answer + invite to retry. Each trajectory has explicit quality and cost trade-offs documented.

Telemetry will include a sampled semantic quality score computed by an internal eval harness; that score will be the primary signal for automated rollback of fallback policies to avoid silent UX degradations.
Cross-region fallbacks require an explicit customer opt-in for data residency-sensitive tenants; default for enterprise customers is opt-out until signed SLI addendum is attached.

SRE to prototype warm-prefix cache approach and report latency delta by 2026-03-12
